identification.summary: XakNet Team is a Russian-language Telegram channel of a self-proclaimed hacktivist group that says it is made up of Russian patriotic volunteers formed in response to Anonymous's declaration of war on Russia (the group's own claim, not independently verified) [S1]. Mandiant reports the moderators advertise multiple domains and social media channels it determined are controlled by the same actors [S1]. Reported activity includes DDoS, website defacement, compromises and hack-and-leak [S1]. Mandiant's April 2024 update re-linked the intrusion activity claimed by these personas from APT28 to APT44 (Sandworm) with high confidence [S1].
identification.firstObserved: 2022-03 (a defaced Ukrainian TV news ticker in early March 2022 was claimed by the moderators) [S1]
identification.notes: Do not merge clusters: Mandiant treats XakNet Team, Infoccentr and CyberArmyofRussia_Reborn as separate Telegram personas it assesses coordinate with APT44, and also notes limited, separate links to KillNet [S1]. The existing record's alias UAC-0100 is not supported here: secondary reporting describes UAC-0100 as a separate fraud-themed cluster and UAC-0106 as XakNet, but I did not open the CERT-UA primary advisories [S7].

attribution.sponsor: Russian GRU (Mandiant assessment: personas coordinate with, or are run by officers of or alongside, APT44/Sandworm) [S1]
attribution.confidence: Moderate (Mandiant) for coordination with APT44, and for moderators being GRU officers or working directly with APT44 operators; Mandiant's 2024 update says the intrusion activity is linked to APT44 with high confidence [S1]. This is a vendor assessment, not a government attribution.
attribution.basis: A unique technical artifact from an APT44 intrusion appeared in an XakNet data leak, indicating APT44 had access to the same network [S1]. In two incidents APT44 wiper attacks (ARGUEPATCH dropping CADDYWIPER) were followed within 24 hours by Telegram leaks of the victims' data [S1]. Mandiant reserves judgement on the groups' composition and exact degree of GRU affiliation [S1].

objectives: Mandiant suggests two possible influence objectives: promoting Russian interests abroad and projecting to domestic audiences that ordinary Russians support the government [S1]. Disruption and leak of Ukrainian government data is the observed operational pattern [S1][S2].

targeting.notes: Claims include a defaced Ukrainian TV news ticker with a fake capitulation message (early March 2022) [S1] and the December 2024 attack on Ukraine's state registers, which XakNet claimed [S2].

capabilities.summary: Publicly visible tradecraft is DDoS, defacement, compromise and hack-and-leak amplified through Telegram, with active solicitation of media coverage [S1]. Mandiant counted at least 16 leaks across the three personas, four of which coincided with APT44 wiping attacks [S1]. Mandiant has observed CADDYWIPER and ARGUEPATCH only in APT44 use, so the destructive capability is attributed to APT44, not the persona [S1].

campaigns.name: Fake capitulation message on Ukrainian TV
campaigns.summary: A Ukrainian news organization's ticker was defaced during a live broadcast with a fake message of capitulation attributed to President Zelenskyy; the XakNet moderators claimed involvement [S1].

campaigns.name: Mandiant links personas to GRU
campaigns.summary: Mandiant published its assessment of moderate-confidence coordination with GRU-sponsored APT44 (then attributed to APT28), citing a leaked APT44 artifact and wiper-then-leak timing [S1].

campaigns.name: Ukraine state registers attack
campaigns.summary: XakNet claimed it breached the National Information Systems and deleted databases and backups; Ukrainian officials called it among the largest cyberattacks, said registration services were disrupted, and denied data was leaked [S2]. Claims of deletion were not independently verified, and attribution to Russian military intelligence in reporting was unconfirmed by officials [S2].

diamond.adversary: Persona of Russian-language Telegram moderators assessed by Mandiant as GRU officers or working directly with APT44 operators (moderate confidence) [S1].
diamond.capability: DDoS, defacement, hack-and-leak and media amplification; destructive tooling (ARGUEPATCH, CADDYWIPER) attributed to APT44 [S1].
diamond.infrastructure: Telegram channels plus multiple domains and social media channels controlled by the same actors [S1].
diamond.socioPolitical: Persona fronts for state-linked operations in the Russia-Ukraine war, claiming volunteer patriotism [S1].
diamond.technology: Telegram for claims and leaks; Windows-network compromise with wiper payloads attributed to APT44 [S1].

gaps: Primary CERT-UA advisories and SSSCIP material could not be opened; alias UAC-0106 and the UAC-0100 mapping are unverified [S7].
XakNet-specific leak counts, infrastructure indicators and tooling are not published in the sources opened [S1].
Claims of the state registers data deletion are unverified and officials disputed data-theft claims [S2].
Whether post-2022 XakNet posts are independent of APT44 is unknown; government attribution not found.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Step 1-2: operating environment is Ukrainian government and media networks, with spillover risk to states supporting Ukraine [S1][S2]. Step 3: the persona is an influence front that amplifies state-linked intrusions; leaks may follow wiper activity within 24 hours [S1]. MLCOA: continued Telegram-announced leak and disruption claims against Ukrainian public-sector systems [S2]. MDCOA: destructive wiper activity against critical registries paired with claims of mass data deletion [S1][S2]. Candidate indicators: Telegram claims preceding or following outages, domains tied to the persona, and wiper artifacts matching APT44 [S1].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. Situational awareness: monitor persona channels for claims and treat them as potential cover for GRU operations, validating against victim telemetry [S1]. Authorities: attribution to a state is a vendor assessment, so response actions need separate government attribution [S1]. Mission assurance: backups held offsite were reportedly claimed deleted in 2024, so verify backup isolation for registry-type services [S2]. Coordination: share indicators with Ukrainian and allied CERT partners and track APT44 reporting [S1].

provenance.importedSummary: XakNet is a self-proclaimed hacktivist group that has targeted Ukraine. They claim to be comprised of Russian patriotic volunteers and have conducted various threat activities, including DDoS attacks, compromises, data leaks, and website defacements. They coordinate their operations with other hacktivist groups and have connections to APT28, a cyber espionage group sponsored by the GRU.
